content.value_statement: Curriculum teams often assign skill levels with vague labels that are hard to assess. This skill maps skills to CEFR, Bloom's taxonomy, and DigComp with measurable indicators and progression checks.
actual_capabilities: Map curriculum skills to CEFR levels from A1 through C2.
Align skills with Bloom's taxonomy cognitive demands.
Use DigComp concepts for digital competence mapping.
Create measurable indicators for each proficiency level.
Check that skill progressions do not regress across lessons.
limitations: It provides curriculum reasoning, not official CEFR certification.
It needs clear lesson goals and learner context for accurate mapping.
It cannot validate real learner performance without assessment evidence.
It may need educator review for domain-specific standards.

use_cases.title: Plan a Course Skill Map
use_cases.description: Turn a list of course skills into a structured progression with levels, prerequisites, and measurable outcomes.

use_cases.title: Improve Assessment Alignment
use_cases.description: Match quiz, project, and rubric expectations to the intended proficiency level for each skill.

use_cases.title: Audit Learning Progression
use_cases.description: Find skills that regress, repeat without growth, or appear before their prerequisites are taught.

prompt_templates.title: Map One Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner use for a single learning objective.
prompt_templates.prompt: Map this skill to CEFR, Bloom's taxonomy, and DigComp where relevant: [skill]. Include measurable indicators and one assessment idea.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Lesson Progression
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate use for several lessons in a unit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these lesson skills and assign proficiency levels. Check that the sequence moves from easier to harder work without regression: [lesson list].

prompt_templates.title: Design Level-Specific Assessments
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate use for rubric or test design.
prompt_templates.prompt: For this skill and target level, create assessment tasks that distinguish A1, A2, B1, and B2 performance: [skill and context].

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Full Curriculum Map
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced use for a multi-chapter curriculum.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this curriculum skill map for naming consistency, prerequisites, progression, cognitive load, and measurable indicators. Recommend specific fixes: [curriculum map].

output_examples.input: Skill: write a useful software specification for a small feature.
output_examples.output: The skill maps to B1 when learners can independently write a complete specification for a real feature. A suitable assessment asks them to produce acceptance criteria, constraints, and success checks for a realistic request.

output_examples.input: A unit introduces decorators at A2, then reviews function syntax at A1 in the next lesson.
output_examples.output: The sequence likely regresses. Move the function syntax foundation before decorators, or raise the later lesson into a review task that supports the A2 objective.

output_examples.input: Need a rubric for comparing weak and strong requirements.
output: A1: Recognizes whether a requirement is measurable.
A2: Revises a simple vague requirement into a measurable one.
B1: Writes complete requirements for a real feature.
B2: Critiques tradeoffs between competing requirement styles.

best_practices: Provide the learner audience, time available, and prerequisites before asking for levels.
Ask for measurable indicators, not only a CEFR or Bloom label.
Review the full sequence for progression and prerequisite gaps.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to assign official credentials without validated assessments.
Do not ask for a level from a vague skill name alone.
Do not accept a progression that moves from advanced work back to basic foundations without explanation.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses CEFR proficiency levels, Bloom's taxonomy, and DigComp concepts to reason about skill progression.

faq.question: Can it create assessment ideas?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest assessment formats and measurable indicators that match a target proficiency level.

faq.question: Is this an official CEFR certification tool?
faq.answer: No. It helps with curriculum design and alignment, but it does not issue official credentials.

faq.question: What input works best?
faq.answer: A clear skill description, learner profile, lesson sequence, available time, and existing prerequisites produce the best results.

faq.question: Can it find curriculum coherence problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It can flag regressions, missing prerequisites, inconsistent names, isolated skills, and vague indicators.

faq.question: Does it work outside language learning?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill applies CEFR-style proficiency reasoning to coding, digital skills, professional skills, and other learning domains.
